name: TraumaCore
teaser: TraumaCore is a configurable damage and injury overhaul for SPT
description:
TraumaCore

TraumaCore is a configurable damage and injury overhaul for SPT. It makes the path a bullet takes through the body matter: armor, penetration, wound depth, bullet size, bones, organs, fragmentation, bleeding, and treatment all contribute to the result.

TraumaCore can make combat more lethal even though penetrating shots deal less damage immediately. A survivor may leave the fight with several wounds and continue losing health until those wounds clot or are treated.

The default setup is intended to remain understandable and playable. AI uses the complete anatomical system, while the most sudden player organ deaths are disabled by default. Player and AI behavior can be configured separately in F12.

Core features

  • Wound depth determines immediate damage and delayed blood loss.
  • Bullet size, speed, mass, penetration, and travel through the body affect wound severity.
  • Light and heavy wounds stack, display live HP loss per second, and naturally clot over time.
  • Internal brain, heart, spine, skull, rib, and limb-bone anatomy makes precise shot placement matter.
  • Brain and upper-spine hits can be fatal; heart hits cause severe permanent hemorrhaging.
  • Bullets can stop inside the body, exit through it, strike bones, or fragment into multiple wound paths.
  • Blocked rounds can cause bruising, movement penalties, reduced stamina recovery, and impact shock.
  • Wound-driven blood sprays, corpse bleeding, custom blood decals, and throttled pain feedback.
  • The death screen shows impact locations, wound paths, direct damage, bleeding, and blood-loss statistics.
  • Corpses can be inspected for wounds and dragged using ragdoll physics.

How a shot is resolved

TraumaCore keeps EFT’s armor decision. EFT still determines whether the armor blocks or penetrates the round using its normal ammunition, armor class, material, coverage, durability, and penetration rules.

If the shot penetrates, TraumaCore uses EFT’s post-armor damage and builds a wound from the actual hit direction and body-part geometry. It considers:

  • How far the projectile can penetrate into tissue
  • How much of the body part it actually crosses
  • Bullet diameter, speed, mass, and penetration power
  • Whether it hits ribs, the skull, the spine, or a limb bone
  • Whether it stops inside the body or creates an exit wound
  • Whether the projectile fragments and creates additional wound paths

Wound depth controls both immediate damage and delayed bleeding. A shallow edge hit still deals meaningful damage, but a deeper center hit reaches full wound strength. Full strength is reached after crossing roughly 75% of the body part’s center-line depth, so shots near the edge do not need to cross the entire model to count properly.

The formula used for these calculations are simple and not made to simulate real ballistics but should make rounds feel more impactful depending on shot placement

Direct damage and total wound damage

A penetrating hit is divided into two parts:

  • Direct damage is applied immediately.
  • Wound damage is delivered gradually through bleeding.

Direct damage scales with wound depth and has a minimum floor, so even a graze matters. Deeper wounds move toward the configured full direct-damage value.

The remaining damage is assigned to the wound’s bleed budget. With the recommended defaults, a complete wound is intended to deal slightly more total damage than the equivalent EFT hit, but much of that damage is delayed. This gives the victim time to react, retreat, or use medical supplies.

Both the immediate-damage fraction and full-wound total damage can be adjusted in F12.

Wounds and bleeding

Every penetrating wound is evaluated as either light or heavy using its depth, projectile diameter, and impact velocity.

  • Multiple wounds stack independently.
  • Larger and deeper wounds begin with a higher damage rate.
  • Exit wounds and fragmentation can increase wound severity.
  • Normal wounds lose strength over time and eventually clot naturally.
  • The first few seconds reduce bleed damage quickly, followed by a slower decline.
  • Each body part displays a native EFT Light Bleeding or Heavy Bleeding effect that shows bleed per second and time remaining on hover.

Treatment

Normal EFT medical items treat TraumaCore wounds through new timer reductions instead of instant removals.

  • Treating a light bleed advances that wound about 90% toward clotting.
  • Treating a heavy bleed advances it about 99% toward clotting.
  • Blood-loss-blocking stims clear existing non-heart bleeding.
  • While a blood-loss blocker is active, applicable treatable bleed damage is reduced by 50%.

Anatomical hitboxes

TraumaCore adds smaller internal targets that follow the character’s animated body:

  • Upper and lower brain
  • Heart
  • Cervical or upper spine
  • Thoracic or lower spine
  • Ribcage and skull resistance
  • arm and leg bones

These are internal targets, not replacements for the entire head or chest. A face hit that misses the brain is not automatically a brain hit, and a chest hit must physically reach the heart before it can damage it.

Fragmentation

TraumaCore can replace EFT’s single abstract fragmentation result with visible wound paths.

When a round fragments inside tissue, it splits into two or three paths within a limited cone. Each path has less remaining penetration than the original projectile, but the combined wound receives additional damage and may create multiple exits. Armor performance can influence the fragmentation chance after penetration.

Custom fragmentation can be disabled separately in F12 if you would not like ammo to randomly do more damage than you could expect

Bruising

Rounds stopped by armor can apply a temporary bruise. Stronger blocked hits create a stronger penalty, and repeated impacts can stack it.

Bruising lasts about 15 seconds and gradually fades. At maximum strength it can reduce movement speed by up to 15% and stamina recovery by up to 30%.

Impact shock

Taking bullet damage can apply a short Impact shock effect. Repeated hits build a peripheral-vision vignette and refresh a brief native Pain marker. This represents the immediate pressure and disorientation of being hit without creating a custom saved health effect.

Blood, audio, and hit presentation

  • Blood originates from wound entry and exit locations visible in-raid.
  • Fragment paths can create blood from more than one opening.
  • Wound blood output weakens as the wound clots.
  • EFT blood decals remain available longer so you can track blood on the ground.
  • Bleed-out deaths can use agony or death voice lines appropriate to the wound.

Procedural blood, expanded decals, and trauma audio/screen effects each have their own F12 toggle.

Death-screen wound report

TraumaCore expands the raid-end damage screen to explain what happened rather than showing only a damage total.

The report can show:

  • Entry, stopping, exit, and fragment locations on each body part
  • The final hit and the sequence of earlier impacts
  • Direct damage and light/heavy bleed damage
  • Total bleed drain, observed bleed duration, and average HP lost per second
  • Wound depth, penetration, impacted anatomy, and projectile-path details

Corpse wound inspection

corpses receive an INSPECT WOUNDS interaction. Inspection opens a dedicated view of the actual EFT corpse ragdoll and allows the body to be examined more closely.

Optional overlays show:

  • Recorded projectile trajectories
  • TraumaCore organ locations
  • Ragdoll and body anchors used to understand the hit location

Corpse dragging

corpses also receive a DRAG BODY interaction.

Dragging:

  • prevents sprinting, and reduces movement speed while active.

Default balance

Anatomical trauma is enabled for both players and AI by default.

For AI and Scavs, the brain, heart, cervical spine, and thoracic spine are all enabled.

For players:

  • Thoracic-spine fractures are enabled.
  • Fatal brain hits are disabled.
  • Heart hemorrhage is disabled.
  • Fatal cervical-spine hits are disabled.

This gives AI the complete anatomical system while reducing unavoidable instant or delayed player deaths from incoming fire. All player and AI organ settings can be changed independently.

Configuration

Press F12 and select TraumaCore to configure the mod.

The menu contains:

  • A Restore Recommended Defaults button at the top
  • Main feature toggles
  • Direct and total-damage balance
  • Separate player and AI anatomical systems
  • Natural clot time
  • Damage linkage and blacked-part retention
  • Blood and presentation options
  • Debug visualization and effect-testing tools

After updating or experimenting with settings, use Restore Recommended Defaults to return every active setting to the balance shipped with the current version.
